parsed.draft_response:
apologetic

Thanks for flagging this—I'm sorry the restored project is still missing required files and comments, especially with a Monday client launch.

To help our engineering team investigate the restore result and determine what content is missing, please reply with the following details:
1) Project identifier/link (project ID or URL) and the workspace/account name.
2) The approximate time the project was deleted and the time you performed “Restore” (including timezone if possible).
3) Which specific items are missing: file names/paths or IDs, and the comment text and/or comment IDs (even a short list is fine).
4) Confirmation on whether the restore action reported success and whether there were any errors/warnings during restore.
5) Whether the missing items are completely absent or only partially missing (and if they reappear/re-appear on refresh).
6) Any changes made after restore (e.g., re-uploads, edits, additional deletions, imports).

Once we have this, we’ll escalate to engineering for human review of the restore contents and help you understand the fastest path to recover what’s needed for your deliverables.

In the meantime, if you have any local copies, exports, or versions from before deletion, please share/retain them for contingency.
promised_actions: Escalate the case to engineering for human review
safety_notes: Do not promise data recovery or restoration of missing items; request missing details to support investigation.
Avoid claiming a root cause, SLA, or refund; provide an escalation acknowledgement only.
